results.title: role attributes: who bypasses RLS
results.detail: query endpoint runs as postgres. anon: super=false bypassrls=false; authenticated: super=false bypassrls=false; authenticator: super=false bypassrls=false; postgres: super=false bypassrls=true; service_role: super=false bypassrls=true; supabase_admin: super=true bypassrls=true; supabase_auth_admin: super=false bypassrls=false.

results.title: FORCE on a postgres-owned table: postgres still reads (BYPASSRLS)
results.detail: postgres (owner, bypassrls=true) read 2 rows with RLS on and no policy, and 2 after FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. On this platform the default owner bypasses RLS, so FORCE changes nothing for a backend that connects as postgres.

results.title: FORCE binds a table owner that cannot bypass RLS
results.detail: owner sec17_owner (NOBYPASSRLS) read 2 rows with RLS on and no policy; 0 after FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.

results.title: service_role via REST under FORCE still reads every row
results.detail: service_role GET -> 200, 2 rows. FORCE has no effect on a BYPASSRLS role.
